context: Theorem 6 There exists a constant c such that any algorithm which outputs a spanning tree T of (X , d) such that E [w(T )] ≤ c log n · minT ′ w(T ′ ) in the weak-strong oracle model (with corruption probability δ = 1/3), must make at least Ω(n) queries to the strong oracle. We conjecture that the lower bound from Theorem 6 is tight, and that an algorithm exists with no strong oracle queries and a O(log n) approximation.
